Note::TexAccessor::symbols¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::symbols() const

Inventory Control Words And Operators¶

symbols() extracts every alphabetic TeX control word together with the ASCII operators + - * / = < > ^ from complete math regions. It is the broadest lexical inventory in this tranche: \sin, \alpha, and a project-local \foo are all symbols, with their leading backslash retained.

The method does not classify or deduplicate. Use math_funcs() or greek() for known semantic subsets, and ops() for the narrower operator vocabulary. Arguments are scanned independently, so \frac{x}{y} contributes \frac but x and y are available through ids(), not this operation. Control symbols such as \% are not alphabetic control words and are not returned.

Only complete anonymous math delimiters establish the search region. Escaped dollars and prose are ignored. Tokens preserve source order and repetitions; offsets preserve input-cell ownership. Undefined input propagates and non-text input throws.

Example 1: A Broad Symbol Stream¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(prose \alpha; $x + \sin(\alpha) = 2.5$)",
        R"(\[\beta \leq y^2\] and \(\sqrt{z}\))",
        R"(escaped \$7)", R"($$\argmax_x f(x) \approx 10$$)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().symbols();
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[10], dim=1, numel=10, encoding=utf8)
["+", "\\sin", "\\alpha", "=", "\\beta", "\\leq", "^", "\\sqrt", "\\argmax", "\\approx"]

Example 2: Rank-Two Ownership¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (auto value : offsets) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

0 4 8 8 10

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().symbols().tokens().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().symbols();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "symbols Int64: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

false
symbols Int64: rejected
